description: Check whether a dashboard can be owned by the current user.

examples.user_query: Check whether I can take ownership of the dashboard with ID '12345abcde'.
examples.notes: This checks if the dashboard with the specified ID can be owned by the current user. Useful for determining ownership eligibility before attempting to claim it.

examples.user_query: Am I allowed to own the dashboard with ID '67890fghij'?
examples.notes: This verifies whether the user has the ability to own the dashboard with the given ID. Typically used in workflows involving dashboard ownership changes.

examples.user_query: Is it possible for me to own the dashboard with ID 'abc123xyz'?
examples.notes: This call determines if the current user can take ownership of the specified dashboard. Useful for validating permissions before proceeding with ownership transfer.

description: Export a dashboard definition using the Sisense admin export endpoint.

examples.user_query: Export the definition of dashboard 5f7d3b2e4c8b9a0012345678.
examples.notes: This call exports the definition of the dashboard with the ID '5f7d3b2e4c8b9a0012345678', which might represent a sales dashboard. Use this to retrieve the dashboard's structure and configuration.

examples.user_query: I need to back up the marketing dashboard configuration. How do I do that?
examples.notes: This call retrieves the definition of the dashboard with the ID '6a8e4f9d5b7c2a0098765432', which could be a marketing dashboard. This is useful for creating a backup of the dashboard's settings and layout.

examples.user_query: Can I get the layout and widgets of the executive overview dashboard?
examples.notes: This call exports the definition of the dashboard with the ID '7b9f5c1d6e8a3b0043210987', potentially representing an executive overview dashboard. Use this to access details like widgets, layout, and filters.

description: Retrieve all dashboards from the Sisense server.

examples.user_query: List all dashboards available on the Sisense server.
examples.notes: This call retrieves all dashboards accessible to the user, including their metadata.

examples.user_query: I need to fetch all dashboards to review their configurations.
examples.notes: Use this to get a complete list of dashboards for auditing or configuration review purposes.

examples.user_query: Can I get a list of all dashboards owned by me?
examples.notes: This retrieves all dashboards, including those owned by the user, using the admin endpoint.

description: Retrieve a specific dashboard by its ID.

dashboard_id.description: The ``oid`` of the dashboard to retrieve.

examples.user_query: Fetch the dashboard with ID '5f7d3a2e4b8c9a0012345678'.
examples.notes: This call retrieves the dashboard with the specified ID. Use this when you need details about a specific dashboard.

examples.user_query: I need to fetch the dashboard with the ID '63a1b2c3d4e5f67890123456'. How do I do that?
examples.notes: This retrieves the dashboard corresponding to the given ID. Useful for accessing dashboard metadata or verifying its existence.

examples.user_query: Can you get me the dashboard with ID '7e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f56789012'?
examples.notes: This call fetches the dashboard identified by the provided ID. Ideal for retrieving specific dashboards for review or updates.

description: Retrieve a specific dashboard by its name.

dashboard_name.description: Title of the dashboard to retrieve.

examples.user_query: Find the dashboard named 'Sales Performance Overview'.
examples.notes: This retrieves the dashboard titled 'Sales Performance Overview', typically used to analyze sales KPIs and trends.

examples.user_query: Get the dashboard called 'Marketing Campaign Analysis'.
examples.notes: Use this to fetch the 'Marketing Campaign Analysis' dashboard, which might contain insights on campaign performance and ROI.

examples.user_query: Retrieve the dashboard with the name 'Executive Summary'.
examples.notes: This call is useful for accessing the 'Executive Summary' dashboard, often used for high-level business reporting.

description: Retrieve widget definitions from an admin export of the dashboard.

examples.user_query: List the widgets in the dashboard titled 'Sales Overview'.
examples.notes: This retrieves all widget definitions from the 'Sales Overview' dashboard using its title as a reference.

examples.user_query: Can you list the widgets in the dashboard with ID '63a9f0ea7bb9805e7e5e1f7c'?
examples.notes: This fetches widget definitions from the dashboard identified by its unique 24-character ID.

examples.user_query: I need to check the widgets in the 'Marketing Performance' dashboard. Can you help?
examples.notes: This retrieves widget definitions from the 'Marketing Performance' dashboard using its title as the reference.

description: Retrieve dashboards visible to the authenticated user.

fields.description: Subset of fields to include in the response (for example ``["oid", "title", "owner"]``). When omitted, all fields are returned.

examples.user_query: Show me the dashboards I own with their titles and IDs.
examples.notes: This call retrieves only the 'oid' and 'title' fields for dashboards visible to the authenticated user. Use this to get a concise list of dashboard identifiers and names.

examples.user_query: I need to see all dashboards shared with me, including their owners and titles.
examples.notes: This call fetches the 'title' and 'owner' fields for dashboards accessible to the user. Useful for understanding who owns the dashboards shared with you.

examples.user_query: Get all available details for dashboards I can access.
examples.notes: This call retrieves all fields for dashboards visible to the authenticated user. Use this when you need comprehensive dashboard details without filtering specific fields.

description: Import one or more dashboards via the bulk import endpoint.

action.description: Conflict behavior for dashboards whose ``oid`` already exists. One of ``"skip"``, ``"overwrite"``, or ``"duplicate"``. Default is ``"skip"``.

examples.user_query: Import dashboards dashboard_123 'Sales Overview' and dashboard_456 'Marketing Performance', skipping any that already exist.
examples.notes: This call imports multiple dashboards and skips any that already exist in the target environment.

examples.user_query: How can I import dashboards and overwrite any existing ones with the same IDs?
examples.notes: This call imports the specified dashboards and overwrites any existing dashboards with matching IDs.

examples.user_query: I want to import dashboards but create duplicates if they already exist. How can I do that?
examples.notes: This call imports the specified dashboards and creates duplicates for any dashboards with matching IDs.

description: Move a dashboard into a folder.

examples.user_query: Move dashboard dashboard_12345 into folder folder_67890.
examples.notes: This moves the 'Sales Overview' dashboard into the 'Q4 Reports' folder. Use this when reorganizing dashboards into specific folders.

examples.user_query: I need to transfer the 'Marketing Performance' dashboard to the 'Archived Dashboards' folder. How do I do that?
examples.notes: This transfers the 'Marketing Performance' dashboard to the 'Archived Dashboards' folder. Useful for archiving older dashboards.

examples.user_query: Can I move the 'Executive Summary' dashboard to the 'Leadership Reports' folder?
examples.notes: This action relocates the 'Executive Summary' dashboard into the 'Leadership Reports' folder. Ideal for organizing dashboards by audience.

examples.user_query: Publish the dashboard with ID 'dashboard_12345'.
examples.notes: This call republishes the specified dashboard with admin access enabled. Use this when the caller has access but is not the owner.

examples.user_query: Force publish the dashboard 'sales_dashboard_2023' after script updates.
examples.notes: This call forces the republishing of the dashboard, typically used after updates to scripts or configurations.

examples.user_query: Republish the dashboard 'marketing_dashboard' without admin access.
examples.notes: This call republishes the dashboard without admin access. Use this when the caller is the owner or already has sufficient permissions.

dashboard_id.description: The ``oid`` of the dashboard to rename.

examples.user_query: Rename dashboard 62f1a2b3c4d5e6f7890abc12 to 'Q3 Sales Performance'.
examples.notes: This renames the dashboard with the specified ID to 'Q3 Sales Performance'. Use this when updating the title to reflect a new reporting period or focus.

examples.user_query: Can I change the name of the 'Marketing Overview' dashboard to '2023 Marketing Strategy'?
examples.notes: This updates the title of the 'Marketing Overview' dashboard to '2023 Marketing Strategy'. Useful for aligning dashboard names with updated organizational goals.

examples.user_query: I need to rename the 'Executive Summary' dashboard to 'Monthly Executive Summary'. How can I do that?
examples.notes: This renames the 'Executive Summary' dashboard to 'Monthly Executive Summary'. Ideal for clarifying the dashboard's purpose or frequency.

description: Resolve a dashboard reference (ID or name) to a concrete dashboard ID and title.

dashboard_ref.description: Dashboard reference to resolve. This can be either an ID or a name.

examples.user_query: Resolve 'Sales Overview' to its dashboard ID and title.
examples.notes: This resolves the dashboard name 'Sales Overview' to its corresponding ID and title. Use this when you know the dashboard name but need its ID.

examples.user_query: Can you find the dashboard with the ID '5f8d04b2c9a123456789abcd'?
examples.notes: This resolves the dashboard ID '5f8d04b2c9a123456789abcd' to its corresponding title. Use this when you have the ID but want to confirm its title.

examples.user_query: I need the details for the dashboard called 'Marketing Performance'.
examples.notes: This resolves the dashboard name 'Marketing Performance' to its ID and title. Use this when you know the dashboard name but need its metadata.
